@context.vis.toolbar: Toolbar menu holding Hide, Isolate, See-through and Show all.
@context.vis.hidden.count: Status line after hiding; {n} = how many elements were just hidden, {total} = how many are hidden now.
@context.ifc.notdrawn.count: One line of the file panel; {text} = what the IFC engine could not draw (in English, from the engine), {n} = how many times.

@context.walk.pad: Label of the group of on-screen buttons that walk through the model on a touch screen.
@context.rvt.note.unreadable: Note on a partly read Revit file; {stream} = internal stream name (e.g. BasicFileInfo), {error} = the reason.
@context.rvt.err.truncated: {size} and {need} are file sizes already formatted, e.g. "12.3 MB".
@context.rvt.err.truncated.unreadable: {size} and {need} are file sizes already formatted, e.g. "12.3 MB".
@context.rvt.why.chain_short: Reason a stream of a cut-off Revit file is missing, shown after the stream name.
@context.rvt.why.index_missing: Reason a stream of a cut-off Revit file is missing, shown after the stream name.
@context.rvt.why.data_missing: Reason a stream of a cut-off Revit file is missing, shown after the stream name.
@context.rvt.why.place_missing: Reason a stream of a cut-off Revit file is missing, shown after the stream name.
@context.rvt.kind.project: Kind of Revit file (.rvt), shown on the file card.
@context.rvt.kind.family: Kind of Revit file (.rfa, a component), shown on the file card.
@context.rvt.zip.not_zip: Technical reason, lower case, shown after "could not be read:".
@context.rvt.zip.method: Technical reason, lower case; {method} = a number.
@context.busy.wait: Status line when the person asks for something while the app is still busy with the previous request.
@context.folder.listing: Status line while the browser lists a folder's files; {n} = how many so far, {count} = the same number formatted.
@context.folder.recent.reopen: Button in the list of recently opened folders; {name} = the folder's name.
@context.folder.recent.forget: Tooltip and label of the x button that removes a folder from the recent list; {name} = the folder's name.

@context.dialog.cancel: Button that closes a dialog without doing anything.
@context.open.reading: Status line; {file} = the file name, {size} = its size already formatted ("12.5 MB").
@context.open.unsupported: Error; {ext} = the file extension with its dot, e.g. .ifczip.
@context.folder.read: Status line after a folder is read (keep "Read the folder" first in English); {s} = seconds, {models} and {files} = folder.n.models and folder.n.files.
@context.folder.n.models: Part of folder.read; {n} = number of models, {count} = the same number formatted.
@context.folder.n.files: Part of folder.read; {n} = number of files, {count} = the same number formatted.
@context.info.h.folder: Heading of the left panel's facts box while a folder is open.
@context.info.h.file: Heading of the left panel's facts box while a file is open.
@context.info.folder: Label in the facts box: the folder's name.
@context.info.file: Label in the facts box: the file's name.
@context.info.problems.none: Value of Problems in the folder facts box when there are none.
@context.info.exported: Label in the IFC facts box: the date the file was exported.
@context.ifc.opened: Status line (keep "Opened" first in English); {file} = file name, {n} = number of elements, {count} = the same formatted, {s} = seconds.
@context.edges.title: Tooltip of the Edges toolbar button.
@context.storey.none: Name of the extra entry in the storey list for elements on no storey.
@context.place.err.write: {what} = the IFC entity name being written, e.g. IFCPROPERTYSET.

@context.ifcedit.err.yesno: Shown when a typed property value is not a yes/no value.

@context.ui.toolbar.view: Screen-reader name of the 3D view toolbar.
@context.ui.view.fit: Toolbar button: fit the whole model in the view, seen from a corner.
@context.ui.view.side: Toolbar button and setting: look at the model from the side.
@context.ui.edges: Toolbar toggle button: show or hide edge lines.
@context.ui.more: Toolbar button that opens a menu of more editing commands.
@context.ui.library: Toolbar button, right-panel tab and its heading: the library of items to place.
@context.ui.equipment: Toolbar button: show the equipment schedule.
@context.ui.updates: Toolbar button: check the library for newer item versions.
@context.ui.sec.cutfrom: Label before the buttons Top, Front, Side and Box on the section bar.
@context.ui.sec.hint: Follows the section offset value: the offset is measured from the bottom of the model.
@context.ui.sec.flip: Button on the section bar: keep the other side of the cut.
@context.ui.v3.iso: Toolbar button: isometric view of the drawing in 3D.
@context.ui.v3.extents: Toolbar button: zoom to the whole drawing.
@context.ui.layers.allon: Button over the layer list: turn every layer on.
@context.ui.layers.alloff: Button over the layer list: turn every layer off.
@context.ui.place.xy: Label of a box where the item's X and Y position is typed, in millimetres.
@context.ui.fmt.folder.name: Heading of the empty-state card that explains opening a whole project folder.
@context.set.view: Settings heading and group name: the view a model opens with.
@context.dwg.skip.missing_block: A kind of drawing object that was not drawn, in the "not drawn" list; {type} = the DWG/DXF object type, e.g. INSERT.
@context.dwg.skip.nested: A kind of drawing object that was not drawn, in the "not drawn" list; {type} = the DWG/DXF object type, e.g. INSERT (a block inside blocks more than 20 levels deep).
@context.dwg.skip.no_picture: A kind of drawing object that was not drawn, in the "not drawn" list; {type} = the DWG/DXF object type, e.g. IMAGE.
@context.dwg.skip.damaged: A kind of drawing object that was not drawn, in the "not drawn" list; {type} = the DWG/DXF object type.
@context.dwg.skip.incomplete: A kind of drawing object that was not drawn, in the "not drawn" list; {type} = the DWG/DXF object type, e.g. POLYGON MESH.
@context.dwg.skip.subdivision: A kind of drawing object that was not drawn, in the "not drawn" list; {type} = MESH (a subdivision mesh).
@context.prop.line: Label in Properties: the element's line number in the IFC file (shown as #123).
@context.prop.change.title: Tooltip of a property value that can be edited; {name} = the property's name.
@context.prop.empty: Shown in place of a property value that is empty.
@context.prop.yes: A Yes/No property value (choice and display).
@context.prop.no: A Yes/No property value (choice and display).
@context.changes.verb.place: Change list verb, used as {verb} in changes.line.
@context.changes.verb.swap: Change list verb, used as {verb} in changes.line.
@context.changes.verb.update: Change list verb, used as {verb} in changes.line.
@context.changes.line: A line of the change list; {verb} = what was done (Placed, Swapped…), {what} = the element's class and name.
@context.changes.was: Second line of a change list entry; {old} = what the element was before.
@context.changes.prop: A line of the change list; {what} = the element, {prop} = the property or attribute changed.

@context.changes.fromto: Second line of a change list entry; {from} and {to} = the old and new values.
@context.save.ifc.count: Save button label; {n} = number of unsaved changes.
@context.edit.undid.step: Status line after Undo; {what} = the change undone (its label or kind).
@context.edit.undid: Status line after Undo; {what} = the property or attribute name.
@context.save.done: Status line; {file} = the new file name, {n} = changes saved, {bytes} = the file size formatted.
@context.info.kind: Label in the file facts box: what kind of Revit file it is (project, family…).
@context.info.read: Label in the file facts box: how much of the file was read ({read} of {size}).
@context.info.complete: Label in the file facts box: whether the file is complete.
@context.rvt.release: The program release a file was saved in; {release} = its year.
@context.rvt.complete.no: Value of Complete for a cut-off file; {size} and {expected} = sizes formatted.
@context.rvt.opened: Status line after opening a Revit file (keep "Opened" first in English); {file} = file name.
@context.rvt.back: Link back to the folder report; {name} = the folder's name.
@context.rvt.kind.release: Card line; {kind} = the kind of file, {release} = the program's release year.
@context.rvt.sec.familygroup: Card section heading; {group} = a parameter group name read from the file.
@context.rvt.link.at: Where a linked file was found; {where} = rvt.link.*, {path} = its path in the folder.
@context.rvt.contents.complete: Value of List of contents: the file's directory is complete.
@context.rvt.f.streams: Label: the parts (streams) of the file recovered.
@context.equip.every.sheet: Choice in the equipment schedule's list picker: equipment on every sheet of the drawing.
@context.equip.every.storey: Choice in the equipment schedule's list picker (IFC models): equipment on every storey.
@context.equip.option: One choice in the equipment list picker; {label} = the choice (a sheet or storey name), {count} = how many items it has.
@context.equip.count.match: Under the equipment filter; {count} = items shown, {query} = the words typed in the filter.
@context.equip.col.where: Column header: the sheets that show the item (a button that jumps there), or whether a linked file is in the folder.
@context.equip.modelonly: In the Where column: the item is in model space and on no sheet.
@context.equip.tags: Under the Where button: how many tags (placements) this item number has.
@context.equip.show.title: Tooltip of the Where button; {no} = the item number.
@context.equip.intro: {count} = how many equipment tags were read from the drawing.
@context.folder.status.ok: Pill on a model file: the file is complete.
@context.folder.status.some: Status pill of a model: {count} of its copies are incomplete (the card still opens a complete one).
@context.folder.link.found: Pill on a linked file: found in the opened folder.
@context.folder.link.found_by_name: Pill on a linked file: a file with the same name was found elsewhere in the folder.
@context.folder.role.linked: Note under a model; {models} = the models that link it. It is background for them.
@context.folder.role.family: Note under a model: the file is a family, i.e. one part or component.
@context.folder.kind: Small label over the folder name in the folder report; also the folder name when the browser gives none.
@context.folder.starthere: Badge and heading of the model the report suggests opening first.
@context.folder.copies.main: Copies column: the main file plus {count} numbered backups.
@context.folder.copies.all: Summary of a fold-out list of every copy of a model (main file and backups).
@context.folder.links.of: Links found column; {found} linked files found of {needed} that should be in the folder.
@context.folder.main.truncated.expected: {size} = the file's size, {expected} = the size its contents say it should have at least.
@context.folder.main.best: {file} = the backup's file name, {date} = when it was saved.
@context.folder.copy.main: Small note beside one copy in the list of copies: this is the main file.
@context.folder.copy.newest: Small note beside one copy in the list of copies: the newest complete copy.
@context.folder.file.meta: Beside a file name: {size} = its size, {date} = when it was last saved.
@context.folder.col.savedin: Column header: the program release the model was saved in.
@context.folder.col.links: Column name on narrow screens (same column as "Links found").
@context.folder.cad.meta.linked: {models} = the models that link this drawing.
@context.folder.aside.title: Heading of the folder report's part listing files that were not read.
@context.folder.aside.other.more: {list} = the first 40 file names, {n} = how many more were left out.
@context.folder.why.newest.date: A reason for the suggested model; {date} = when it was last saved.
@context.folder.why.linked: {names} = model file names, joined by commas; {n} = how many.
@context.folder.toomany: {max} = the most files a folder may have, formatted.
@context.dwg.coords: Pointer position under the drawing; {x} and {y} = coordinates (keep the two spaces before Y).
@context.equip.ringed.cat: Status line after jumping to an item; {no} = item number, {category} = its category, {sheet} = the sheet's name.
@context.equip.downloaded: Status line; {file} = the CSV's name, {n} = rows, {count} = the same formatted.
@context.dwg.img.notfound: Status pill of a picture whose file was not found.
@context.dwg.format.release: Facts box value; {release} = the CAD program release the file was saved for, {tag} = the file's version code (AC1032).
@context.dwg.linked.loaded: Facts box value; {loaded} of {total} linked drawings were found and drawn.
@context.dwg.linked.shown: Status pill of a linked drawing that was found and drawn.
@context.dwg.img.shown: Status pill of a picture that was found and drawn.
@context.dwg.opened: Status line (keep "Opened" first in English); {file} = file name, {s} = seconds.
@context.dwg.unreadable.binary: Error; {file} = file name, {why} = the reason (another message).
@context.dwg.unreadable: Error; {file} = file name, {format} = the file's version code or DWG/DXF.
@context.dwg.addedbyyou: Where a linked file came from: the person added it with Add linked drawings.
@context.dwg.tab.equipment: Tab above the drawing; {n} = number of equipment items (formatted).
@context.dwg.tab.fit: Toolbar button: zoom to show the whole drawing.
@context.sec.hint.top: Words after the offset box of the section bar: how the offset is measured.
@context.sec.hint.front: Words after the offset box of the section bar: how the offset is measured.
@context.sec.hint.side: Words after the offset box of the section bar: how the offset is measured.
@context.sec.ifc.beyond.start: {size} = the model's size along the cut's direction, in metres.
@context.clip.name.libitem: Name of a copied placement whose library item has no name.
@context.clip.unnamed: Name of a copied element that has no name in the model.
@context.clip.note.item_invalid: {error} = the first problem the format check found (technical).
@context.clip.text.head: First line of an element copied as plain text: {cls} = its IFC class without "Ifc" (e.g. Wall), {name} = its name.
@context.clip.text.row: A line of an element copied as plain text: {label} = a field or property name, {value} = its value.
@context.clip.text.description: Field label in an element copied as plain text (the element's description).
@context.lib.license.maker: License badge: the maker's own terms of use.
@context.lib.license.team: License badge: only for the team that owns the item.
@context.lib.err.status: {status} = an HTTP status code number, e.g. 503.
@context.lib.err.format: {errors} = the first problems found, technical, joined with "; ".
@context.lib.source.feed: Where a library item came from (another library feed), in the item's From row.
@context.lib.source.drawing: Where a library item came from (the open drawing), in the item's From row.
@context.lib.sources: Accessible name of the row of library source buttons.
@context.lib.src.this: Library source button: the blocks of the drawing that is open.
@context.lib.src.files: Library source button: make items from files on this computer.
@context.lib.src.feed: Library source button: other libraries (feeds) the user added.
@context.lib.notes.file: Heading of a fold-out list of notes; {n} = how many.
@context.lib.search: Accessible name of the library search box.
@context.lib.category.option: Category choice; {group} = the category group (e.g. Kitchen), {label} = the category name.
@context.lib.signin.prompt: {link} becomes a link reading lib.signin.link ("Sign in to the library").
@context.lib.feed.intro: The paths in brackets are web API paths: leave them as they are.
@context.lib.feed.remove: Button title; {feed} = the feed's web address.
@context.lib.files.up.y: Choice for which axis points up in a mesh file (glTF, OBJ).
@context.lib.card.version: Version badge on a library card; {version} = the version number.
@context.lib.card.team: Badge on a library card: a team library item.
@context.lib.row.kind: Field label: what kind of item (equipment, furniture…).
@context.lib.row.from: Field label: where the item came from.
@context.lib.body.box: Value of the 3D body field: a simple box.
@context.lib.body.mesh: Value of the 3D body field; {n} = the number of triangles.
@context.lib.withdrawn.reason: {reason} = the reason the library gave, in its own words.
@context.lib.license.heading: Heading of the license box in the item details.
@context.lib.notes: Heading of a fold-out list of notes about the item; {n} = how many.
@context.lib.swap: Button; {name} = the placed item that would be swapped for this one.
@context.lib.block.title.no: Heading of the library box in Properties; {no} = the placed item's number.
@context.lib.block.from.file.name: Where a placed item came from; {file} = the source file's name.
@context.lib.swap.theitem: Stands in for {name} in lib.swap.pick when the element has no name.
@context.lib.swap.pick: Status line; {name} = the placed item being swapped. "Swap … to this" is a button's label in the Library tab.
@context.place.bar.placing: Placing bar; {name} = the library item's name.
@context.place.at: Placing bar readout; {x}, {y} in mm, {rot} = rotation in degrees (keep the two spaces).
@context.place.rot: Placing bar readout before the pointer is on the model; {rot} = rotation in degrees.
@context.place.done: Status line; {name} = the item, {no} = its item number.
@context.swap.done: Status line; {from} = the old item's name, {to} = the new item's name.
@context.credits.line.license: One credit line; {name} = the item's name, {license} = its license's name.
@context.credits.line.file.src: One credit line; {name} = the item's name, {file} = the file it came from.
@context.credits.col.usedas: Column of item numbers the library item is placed as.
@context.lib.version: A library item's version number, as v3.
@context.credits.fromfile: License column value for an item that came from a file (no license).
@context.updates.st.withdrawn: Status pill: the library withdrew this item.
@context.updates.changes: {kinds} = the kinds of change, as the library names them, joined by commas.

@context.edit.redid: Status line after Redo; {what} = the property or attribute name.
@context.edit.copy.item.no: {name} = the library item, {no} = its item number.
@context.edit.copy.toolarge: Added after edit.copy.item when the item cannot be kept for other tabs.
@context.edit.pasted.item: {name} = the item, {no} = its new item number. CadCraft_Placement is a property set's name: keep it as written.
@context.edit.paste.thestorey: Stands in for {storey} in edit.pasted.inplace.* when the storey has no name.
@context.edit.paste.how.name: Fill {how} (after a space) in edit.pasted.inplace.*: why that storey was chosen.
@context.edit.paste.how.elevation: Fill {how} (after a space) in edit.pasted.inplace.*: why that storey was chosen.
@context.edit.paste.how.first: Fill {how} (after a space) in edit.pasted.inplace.*: why that storey was chosen.
@context.edit.pasted.inplace.beside: {name} = the item, {no} = its item number, {storey} = the storey's name, {how} = empty or a space and edit.paste.how.*.
@context.edit.pasted.inplace.same: {name} = the item, {no} = its item number, {storey} = the storey's name, {how} = empty or a space and edit.paste.how.*.

vis.menu.title: Hide, isolate or see through the picked elements
vis.hide.title: Hide the picked elements (H)
vis.isolate.title: Show only the picked elements (I)
vis.ghost.title: Show the picked elements, and everything else see-through (T)
vis.showall.title: Show every element again (Shift+H)
vis.need.pick: Pick one or more elements first (Ctrl+click picks more).

vis.hidden.count.one: Hid {n} element ({total} hidden). Shift+H shows everything again.
vis.hidden.count.other: Hid {n} elements ({total} hidden). Shift+H shows everything again.

vis.isolated.one: Showing only the picked element. Shift+H shows everything again.
vis.isolated.other: Showing only the {n} picked elements. Shift+H shows everything again.

vis.ghosted.one: Showing the picked element, the rest see-through. Clicks go through see-through elements. Shift+H shows everything again.
vis.ghosted.other: Showing the {n} picked elements, the rest see-through. Clicks go through see-through elements. Shift+H shows everything again.

pick.many.hint: Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on a Mac) or Shift+click adds an element or takes it out. Click one on its own to see its properties.
edit.copy.title: Copy the picked elements (Ctrl+C): to paste in this model, and as text for other programs
edit.paste.title: Paste what you copied: it follows the pointer, click where it goes (Ctrl+V)
edit.cut.title: Cut the picked elements: copy them, then delete them (Ctrl+X)
edit.delete.title: Delete the picked elements, with their parts and openings (Delete)
edit.duplicate.title: Copy the picked elements and place the copy where you click (Ctrl+D)
edit.selectall.title: Pick every element that is shown (Ctrl+A)
edit.need.pick: Pick one or more elements first.
edit.refused.spatial: Storeys, spaces, buildings and the site cannot be copied or deleted: pick the elements in them.

edit.refused.some.one: {n} storey or space was left: those cannot be deleted.
edit.refused.some.other: {n} storeys or spaces were left: those cannot be deleted.

edit.paste.nothing: Nothing copied yet: pick one or more elements and Copy them.
edit.paste.textonly: That copy holds text only (made by an earlier BimCraft build). Copy the elements again to paste them.
edit.paste.othermodel: Building elements paste into the model they were copied from ({file}). Placed library items paste into any model.
edit.paste.othertab: Those elements were copied in another tab. Copy them again in this tab to paste them here.

edit.copy.done.one: Copied 1 element. Ctrl+V pastes it where you click, Ctrl+Shift+V beside it.
edit.copy.done.other: Copied {n} elements. Ctrl+V pastes them where you click, Ctrl+Shift+V beside them.

edit.cut.done.one: Cut 1 element. Ctrl+V pastes it where you click; Ctrl+Z puts it back.
edit.cut.done.other: Cut {n} elements. Ctrl+V pastes them where you click; Ctrl+Z puts them back.

edit.delete.done.one: Deleted 1 element. Ctrl+Z puts it back.
edit.delete.done.other: Deleted {n} elements. Ctrl+Z puts them back.

edit.delete.parts.one: 1 part or opening went with it.
edit.delete.parts.other: {n} parts and openings went with them.

edit.paste.start.one: Pasting: click where the copy goes. R turns it, Esc stops.
edit.paste.start.other: Pasting {n} elements: click where the copy goes. R turns them, Esc stops.

edit.duplicate.start.one: Duplicated: click where the copy goes. R turns it, Esc stops.
edit.duplicate.start.other: Duplicated {n} elements: click where the copy goes. R turns them, Esc stops.

edit.paste.done.one: Pasted 1 element (new GlobalId, same geometry and data). Click again for another copy; Ctrl+Z undoes it.
edit.paste.done.other: Pasted {n} elements (new GlobalIds, same geometry and data). Click again for another copy; Ctrl+Z undoes it.

edit.paste.inplace.one: Pasted 1 element where it was cut from. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
edit.paste.inplace.other: Pasted {n} elements where they were cut from. Ctrl+Z undoes it.

edit.paste.beside.one: Pasted 1 element beside the original: the same spot would put two in one place. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
edit.paste.beside.other: Pasted {n} elements beside the originals: the same spot would put two of each in one place. Ctrl+Z undoes it.

dwg.pick.intro: Click an object to see its properties; Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on a Mac) picks more. Esc clears the pick.
dwg.pick.hint: Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on a Mac) adds an object or takes it out. Click one on its own to see its properties.
dwg.pick.back: Esc, or a click on empty space, goes back to what the 3D view shows.
tree.title: Model tree

color.cleared: Colors are back to the model's own.

color.isolated.one: Showing the {n} element with {value}. Shift+H shows everything again.
color.isolated.other: Showing the {n} elements with {value}. Shift+H shows everything again.

edit.need.pick.one: Pick an element in the model first.
edit.need.ifc.paste: Open an IFC model to paste into.
edit.paste.noitem: The copy of {name} came from {file} without its library item (placed in an earlier session, or too large to keep). Place it from the Library tab, or copy it in this model.
edit.paste.noitem.other: The copy of {name} came from another model without its library item (placed in an earlier session, or too large to keep). Place it from the Library tab, or copy it in this model.
edit.copy.noplacement: Could not read that placement back from the model.
edit.copy.item: Copied {name}. Ctrl+V pastes it where you click, Ctrl+Shift+V in place.
edit.copy.item.no: Copied {name} (item {no}). Ctrl+V pastes it where you click, Ctrl+Shift+V in place.
edit.copy.toolarge: The item is too large to share with other tabs; this tab can paste it anywhere.
clip.text.label: Copied text
clip.text.title: Copy the text
clip.text.hint: The browser did not let BimCraft use the clipboard. The text is selected: press Ctrl+C (Cmd+C on a Mac).
edit.paste.item: Pasting {name}: click where the copy goes. R turns it, Tab snaps its back to a wall, Esc stops.
edit.dup.item: Duplicated {name}: click where the copy goes. R turns it, Tab snaps its back to a wall, Esc stops.
edit.pasted.item: Pasted {name} as item {no} (its number is in Properties, CadCraft_Placement). Click again for another copy; Ctrl+Z undoes it.
edit.paste.nostoreys: This model has no storeys to paste on.
edit.paste.how.name: (same storey name)
edit.paste.how.elevation: (nearest storey height: no storey has its name)
edit.paste.how.first: (the lowest storey: the copy says no storey)
edit.pasted.inplace.beside: Pasted {name} in place as item {no} on {storey}{how}, beside the original: the same spot would put two items in one place. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
edit.pasted.inplace.same: Pasted {name} in place as item {no} on {storey}{how}, at the same X, Y and turn. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
set.assist.on: Let AI assistants and scripts use BimCraft
set.assist.hint: An assistant on this computer (Claude and others) reaches BimCraft through CadCraft Studio, only while this is on. Off by default; turning it off disconnects at once.
set.assist.read: Read: find elements and read their properties
set.assist.edit: Change the view: isolate, see-through, hide and show elements (the model itself is never changed)
assist.banner.read: An assistant is connected to BimCraft: {client}. It can find elements and read their properties.
assist.banner.edit: An assistant is connected to BimCraft: {client}. It can find elements, read their properties and change what the view shows.
